sections.normalized_html: The equations [MATH: ax + 4by = 100] and [MATH: 3x - 2by = -10] intersect at the point [MATH: (8, y).] What is the value of [MATH: a?]
sections.readable_text: The equations [MATH: ax + 4by = 100] and [MATH: 3x - 2by = -10] intersect at the point [MATH: (8, y).] What is the value of [MATH: a?]

sections.normalized_html:
Coordinates of the point of intersection [MATH: (8, y)] represent the solution to the following system of linear equations:
[MATH: {ax + 4by = 100; 3x − 2by = − 10]

Since [MATH: (8,y)] is the solution of this system of equations, we first substitute [MATH: x = 8] into the second equation to solve for [MATH: by{:}]
[MATH: 3(8) − 2by|= − 10; 24 − 2by|= − 10; − 2by|= − 34; by|= 17]

Now, we substitute [MATH: x = 8] and [MATH: by = 17] into the first equation to solve for [MATH: a{:}]
[MATH: a(8) + 4(17)|= 100; 8a + 68|= 100; 8a|= 32; a|= 4]

So the value of [MATH: a] is [MATH: 4.]
